A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same TRACE study with complete, matchable scientific content, including Appendices A–F, Tables 1–16, and Figures 1–21. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison despite bibliography reflow.

before.justification: v3 reports original TRACE segmentation experiments, component ablations, boundary-quality measurements, and appendix evaluations covering additional benchmarks and failure cases.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including segmentation comparisons in Tables 1–2 and the extended and failure-domain evaluations in Tables 12–15.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix C retain the same IEP selection, ABDiv boundary extraction, uncertainty masking, one-step distillation objective, and mask-propagation procedure. Algorithms 1–4 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain ImageNet training, VOC/COCO segmentation tasks, the broader UIS and open-vocabulary benchmarks, and satellite and medical evaluations. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods, including MaskCut/ProMerge, panoptic baselines, diffusion and non-diffusion backbones, conventional edge detectors, and appendix comparators. The YOLOE citation attribution changes, but its participation in Figure 9 is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices C/F retain the same training and evaluation procedures, splits, subset sizes, model configurations, preprocessing, and metrics. No new or revised evaluation protocol is documented.

E4.justification: The component, reconstruction-loss, similarity-metric, decoder-capacity, prompt, and uncertainty-masking analyses are retained. IEP distributions, fragmentation examples, and satellite/medical failure analyses also remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain the same general reference to consistency across random seeds in Appendix C.4. Run counts, error bars, confidence intervals, and significance tests are not newly reported or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative examples are unchanged throughout both PDFs. For example, ProMerge+TRACE retains 8.2 AP on COCO 2014 in Table 1(a), and TRACE retains 0.889 ODS in Table 6. Appendix failure results are also identical.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations are retained, including Appendix D's assumptions A.1–A.3, entropy derivation, and inter-step KL/Fisher-information argument. No proof or mathematical reasoning is revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion preserve the same claims about diffusion instance priors, IEP/ABDiv, fast one-step prediction, and downstream segmentation benefits.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and applicability limits are unchanged, including VAE compression of tiny satellite objects and the mismatch between natural-image diffusion priors and histopathology imagery in Section 6 and Appendix E.4.

D1.justification: v4 adds a front-page Project Page address absent from v3, providing new resource-access information. Implementation settings and reproducibility instructions remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish the availability of code or other resources at that address.

R1.justification: Appendix B.3 and the bibliography remove Jo et al. (2022), RecurSeed and EdgePredictMix, from the weakly supervised segmentation literature list. Broader research positioning is unchanged; other reference edits concern retained works' metadata or duplicate entries.

P1.justification: v4 updates conference headers, correspondence details, acknowledgments, and affiliation wording. It standardizes bibliography formatting, consolidates duplicate Ahn et al. (2019) entries, and revises bibliographic metadata. Scientific prose and section organization remain largely identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–21 and Tables 1–16 retain their displays and ordering. The new project-page line changes first-page spacing, while the shortened bibliography reflows the document and moves the appendix one page earlier.

improvement.justification: The front-page project and contact information improves discoverability, while bibliography standardization and removal of the duplicate Ahn reference provide modest editorial benefits. The scientific methods, evidence, theory, and documented limitations remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited to accessibility and presentation.
